problem_type: React Flow canvas context-menu gesture lifecycle regression
symptom: A secondary-button click on blank canvas or on a node no longer opened the add-node or node-action menu in the real macOS Electron build, while the same secondary button still needed to support drag-to-pan.
direct_cause: The React Flow renderer opened menus directly from onPaneContextMenu and onNodeContextMenu instead of using the existing pointer-down, movement-threshold, pointer-up lifecycle that distinguishes a context click from a secondary-button pan.
class_root: The renderer migration preserved the context-menu component but did not preserve its gesture ownership protocol; a structure test checked that the old hook still existed without proving that the active React Flow renderer consumed it.
affected_population: macOS users opening a blank-canvas add menu with a secondary click or Control-click
Users opening node copy, cut, paste, group, or delete actions from the visible node menu
Users who use the secondary mouse button both for context clicks and canvas panning
entry_points: Secondary-button click on React Flow pane
Secondary-button click on a generation node
macOS Control-click on pane or node
Secondary-button drag that must pan without opening a menu
internal_only_reason: The deciding behavior is Nomi's canvas gesture contract and the event ordering of its active Electron renderer. External documentation cannot decide whether Nomi should open a menu or pan after a specific pointer sequence, and the existing real journeys are the authoritative interaction probes.
invariants: The active React Flow renderer prepares a context candidate on pointer-down and commits it only after pointer-up without movement beyond the drag threshold.
A secondary-button drag pans the canvas and suppresses both the native browser menu and the custom Nomi menu.
A node context click preserves an existing multi-selection or selects the clicked node before menu actions run.
Menu pointer-down events do not close the menu before the selected action receives its click.
Structure coverage proves the active renderer imports and wires the shared context-menu lifecycle instead of merely checking dormant source code.

recurrence.reason: Every pane or node secondary-click shares the active renderer lifecycle, and future renderer rewiring could again leave the gesture hook dormant while menus still render.
same_class_scan: Scanned every onContextMenu, onPaneContextMenu, and onNodeContextMenu binding in the generation-canvas renderer.
Scanned the shared context-menu hook entry points for pane clicks, node clicks, Control-click, secondary drag, and multi-selection preservation.
Ran the blank-menu, node-menu, keyboard shortcut, and secondary-button pan Electron journeys against the active React Flow renderer.

prevention.strategy: Make the active React Flow host consume the shared deferred pointer lifecycle and keep menu suppression coupled to the same pan gesture state.

migration: No project or canvas schema migration is required. The change restores transient pointer and menu state only.
residual_risks: Non-pointer keyboard context-menu invocation remains browser-owned because the shared lifecycle intentionally requires a pointer candidate.
Platform-specific event ordering remains covered by the real macOS Electron journeys and the Linux suite will continue to exercise the same renderer path.
